This is the material for the tutorial on contributing to the Stan ecosystem at StanCon 2026.

## Goals {.unnumbered}

By the end of this workshop you should be able to:

+ Explain what Stan is and how the ecosystem is organized
+ Identify which repository matches your skills and interests
+ Follow the contribution workflow for Stan's R packages
+ Make a small, reviewable first contribution

## Prerequisites {.unnumbered}

+ Basic familiarity with Bayesian modeling (helpful but not required)
+ Comfort with either R or Python for the hands-on section
+ A GitHub account

## How to use these materials {.unnumbered}

This repository is a **Quarto book**. The same section files render as:

| Command | Output |
|---------|--------|
| `quarto render` | Full HTML book in `_book/` (notebook/handout) |
| `quarto render --profile slides 02-ecosystem.qmd` | RevealJS slides for one section in `_slides/` |

Each chapter file can be rendered on its own for presenting a single session:

```bash
quarto render --profile slides 02-ecosystem.qmd
```
